correctness.rationale: Oddification \(f(\varepsilon)\mapsto (f(\varepsilon)-f(-\varepsilon))/2\) is an \(L^4\) contraction preserving the first-chaos component. Every odd input has the unique 8-coordinate form \(f=S+\chi T\) with \(S=\sum a_ir_i\) and \(T=\sum b_ir_i\). The exact Walsh fourth-moment difference \(\mathbb E(f^4)-(123/200)\mathbb E(S^4)\) was freshly rebuilt from the stated rational Gram matrices \(M_0,M_1,M_2\) and verified coefficient by coefficient in eight independent variables. Fresh symbolic computation independently evaluated every leading principal minor: all 8 of \(M_0\), 4 of \(M_1\), and 4 of \(M_2\) are strictly positive, so the identity is a genuine sum of squares for all real inputs. The explicit three-coordinate witness \(f=r_1+r_2+r_3+tr_1r_2r_3\) has projected fourth moment 21 and input moment \(21+18t^2+t^4+24t\), proving the lower bound. Numerical approximations are used only for illustration, not certification.
correctness.risk: Only four independent signs over the real scalar field; the exact norm remains unknown.

final_claim: For the real first-chaos Rademacher projection \(R_4\) on \(\{-1,1\}^4\) in \(L^4\), if \(t\) is the unique real root of \(t^3+9t+6=0\), then \(\left(21/(21+18t^2+t^4+24t)\right)^{1/4}\le\|R_4\|\le(200/123)^{1/4}\). The exact norm is not asserted.
